title: Borsuk-Ulam CRT for Squarefree Numbers: Generalization to k Primes
description: Proves that the CRT compatibility for BU dimensions (buDim(pq,d) = max(buDim(p,d), buDim(q,d)) for distinct primes p,q) generalizes to squarefree n = p₁·p₂·…·pₖ. The main result is that buDim(n,d) = sup_{p ∈ primeFactors(n)} buDim(p,d) for ALL n ≥ 2, not just squarefree numbers. This follows immediately from buDim_eq_formula and the definition of buDimFormula. Concrete cases buDim(30,d) = buDim 2 d ⊔ buDim 3 d ⊔ buDim 5 d and buDim(210,d) = buDim 2 d ⊔ … ⊔ buDim 7 d are verified. The general k-prime formula is proved by induction on a Finset of distinct primes.

overview.historicalContext:
The Borsuk-Ulam theorem (1933) classifies maps Sⁿ → Sᵐ by showing that no map sends every point to its antipodal image when n > m. For equivariant BU theory applied to cyclic groups ℤ/nℤ, the BU dimension buDim(n,d) measures the topological complexity. The Chinese Remainder Theorem (CRT) provides the algebraic structure: for coprime m, n, we have ℤ/mnℤ ≅ ℤ/mℤ × ℤ/nℤ, so representations of ℤ/mnℤ factor through the product. This algebraic factorization should be reflected at the level of BU dimensions, giving CRT compatibility.

The semiprime case (n = pq, two distinct primes) was proved in OQ03 (assuming a CRT axiom) and in OQ03-OQ01 (deriving CRT from the formula conjecture). This entry asks whether the same generalization holds for squarefree n = p₁·…·pₖ with k ≥ 3 prime factors. The answer is YES, and the proof reveals something deeper: the equality buDim(n,d) = sup_{p prime, p|n} buDim(p,d) holds for ALL n ≥ 2, not just squarefree numbers.
overview.problemStatement:
**The Open Question**: Does the CRT compatibility buDim(pq, d) ≤ max(buDim(p,d), buDim(q,d)) (for distinct primes p, q) generalize to squarefree n = p₁·p₂·…·pₖ (a product of k distinct primes)?

**Answer**: YES, and the result is stronger than expected. For ALL n ≥ 2:
  buDim(n, d) = n.primeFactors.sup (fun p => buDim p d)
This follows immediately from buDim_eq_formula (which gives the equality for any n ≥ 2) and the definition of buDimFormula. The CRT structure is not special to squarefree numbers — it is encoded in the formula axiom for all composite numbers.
overview.text:
The key insight is that buDimFormula n d is **defined** as n.primeFactors.sup (fun p => buDim p d), and the formula axiom gives buDim n d = buDimFormula n d for all n ≥ 2. So the CRT equality is not an additional theorem — it is the formula itself.

For squarefree n = p₁·…·pₖ (k distinct primes), the prime factor set n.primeFactors = {p₁, …, pₖ}, giving:
  buDim(n, d) = sup({buDim(pᵢ, d)}) = max(buDim(p₁,d), …, buDim(pₖ,d))

The proof of primeFactors(∏ S) = S for a Finset S of primes proceeds by induction: the base case uses Nat.primeFactors_prime (a prime's factorization is a singleton), and the inductive step uses Nat.primeFactors_mul to split the product.
overview.proofStrategy: The main theorem buDim_eq_sup_primeFactors follows in 2 lines: unfold buDimFormula in buDim_eq_formula (the two-sided formula bound). For concrete squarefree numbers (30, 210, 2310), native_decide computes the primeFactors directly. The general k-prime formula buDim_prod_primes_eq uses induction via primeFactors_prod_primes to identify primeFactors(∏ S) = S.

crossReferences.description: Parent: proved CRT for semiprimes (n=pq) with axiom buDim_crt_semiprime. This entry generalizes to squarefree n with k prime factors and proves without that axiom.
Grandparent: defines buDimFormula and proves buDim_eq_formula. The CRT result here is a direct consequence of that formula.

conclusion.summary: The CRT compatibility buDim(n,d) = sup_{prime p|n} buDim(p,d) holds for ALL n ≥ 2 (proved), not just squarefree numbers. For squarefree n = p₁·…·pₖ with distinct primes, this gives buDim(n,d) = max(buDim(pᵢ,d)). The proof uses 0 new axioms beyond the base framework (buDim, buDim_mono, buDim_le_formula). The squarefree generalization to k primes is proved by induction on the Finset of prime factors.
conclusion.implications: The CRT compatibility was previously established case-by-case (semiprime n=pq in OQ03, then proved from formula in OQ03-OQ01). This entry shows the result is not special to 2-prime products: it holds for any composite n and follows directly from the formula axiom. The key structural insight is that buDimFormula is *defined* as the sup over prime factors, so the CRT property is literally built into the formula.
